analysis: The endpoint-only masking trial completed successfully but achieved macro validation HR@10 of 0.4500, below the plan’s stated reference of 0.5613 by 0.1113. Category HR@10: Movies_and_TV 0.520, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.515, Electronics 0.430, CDs_and_Vinyl 0.335. Electronics exceeded the cited parent value of 0.385, but this did not translate into a macro improvement. Endpoint masking aligns training context with inference, yet removes interior-token supervision and reduces targets per sampled history. Reduced supervision is a plausible explanation for the regression, not an established cause. Training curves and parent results for all categories were not supplied. Allocated GPU time was 240.89 seconds.
code_summary: Trains one independent bidirectional masked-item Transformer per category: 64-token windows, 96-dimensional embeddings, two attention blocks with two heads, dropout 0.25, and a normalized output transform. The experimental change masks and supervises only the final item of each sampled window; random endpoint sampling remains. Scores use tied normalized item embeddings, a learned scale, and jointly trained item biases. Training uses cross-entropy with 512 sampled negatives, AdamW, learning-rate warmup, and gradient clipping. Validation selects one checkpoint per category by HR@10, breaking ties with NDCG@10. The generated predictor routes datasets to their single checkpoint and appends a mask after the observed history. Seeds, supplied splits, four-category routing, and trial-local artifacts are retained; no ensemble is used.
